A1.justification: Both PDFs are complete 32-page versions of BRIDGE. The main text, Appendices A–N, equations, 14 tables and 17 figures support reliable comparison, including material relocated between pages.

before.justification: v5 reports original generation and controllability experiments (Tables 1–4), text and multi-agent ablations, and synthetic-data forecasting results (Appendices I and M).

after.justification: v7 retains original generation, human-evaluation, ablation and forecasting results, including two updated human-evaluation scores in Table 3.

M1.justification: The multi-agent template-refinement framework and text/prototype-conditioned diffusion model remain unchanged. Section 4 and Appendix B retain the same loss, prototype assignment, training and inference procedures.

E1.justification: Both versions use AirPassenger/Sunspots for text evaluation, the same 12 generation datasets, Stock/Web for unseen-domain evaluation, and ILI/M4 for downstream forecasting. The added Web description documents an already-evaluated dataset.

E2.justification: Generation comparisons retain TimeVQVAE, TimeGAN, GT-GAN and TimeVAE. The forecasting models, KernelSynth/random-data controls and ablated variants also remain unchanged within their corresponding comparisons.

E3.justification: The ranking-with-ground-truth and three-distractor procedures are already described in v5 Appendix H; v7 clarifies and renames them HE-Rank and HE-Mixed. Splits, training budgets, sequence lengths and forecasting horizons remain unchanged. Newly disclosed imputation details do not establish changed experimental settings.

E4.justification: The text/prototype, text-type, agent-strategy, prototype-count and encoder ablations are retained, alongside the prototype visualizations. Their tested components and configurations remain unchanged; the two Table 3 score updates do not introduce a different analysis.

E5.justification: Uncertainty reporting is retained. Appendix M still describes individual-score t-tests and 1,000-resample bootstrapping for OWA. Table 14 retains the same significance results and threshold; its relocation does not add statistical evidence.

E6.justification: For w/o Text in Table 3, Wind's HE score, renamed HE-Rank, changes from 4.1 to 4.0; Pedestrian's HE@3 score, renamed HE-Mixed, changes from 5.0 to 4.0. These changes preserve the comparison orderings. Other matched table results are unchanged; the PDFs do not explain whether these updates are corrections or reruns.

T1.justification: The problem formulation, denoising objective, prototype-mask and cross-attention equations, and metric definitions remain unchanged across Section 3, Section 4 and Appendices B/G. No theorem or proof is added or revised.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution statements and conclusion retain the same claims about multi-agent dataset construction, text-controlled generation and unseen-domain generalization. The claims of fidelity leadership on 11 of 12 datasets and controllability improvements up to 12% MSE and 6% MAE are unchanged.

C2.justification: Interpretations concerning complementary text/prototype roles, concise descriptions, few-shot generalization and synthetic-data utility are retained. No substantive limitation or applicability boundary is added or removed.

D1.justification: Appendix F.1 adds Web corpus provenance, size/date range and zero imputation, plus NN5 weekday-median imputation information. These newly document retained experiments. Appendix H.1 drops the explicit count of four model-output settings. Hardware, training hyperparameters and code access remain unchanged.

R1.justification: The related-work discussion and reference list remain unchanged, including positioning relative to GenG, Time-MMD and TimeDP. Added dataset-source descriptions do not introduce new research-positioning claims.

P1.justification: v7 locally rewrites the human-evaluation explanation and Appendix F.1 dataset descriptions, renames HE/HE@3 to HE-Rank/HE-Mixed, and updates an author affiliation. The overall section hierarchy and narrative remain intact.

P2.justification: Tables 3–4 receive revised metric labels and smaller typography. Appendix tables and figures reflow, notably moving Table 14 from page 32 to page 28 beside Table 13. No table or figure is added or removed, and the plotted content is retained.

improvement.justification: Appendix F.1 fills documentation gaps concerning dataset provenance and missing-value handling, while Section 5.1.3 and Appendix H clarify the existing human-ranking procedure. These provide a modest net gain in reproducibility and clarity. The scientific evidence remains largely unchanged; smaller typography in Tables 3–4 and the omitted explicit model-output count are limited tradeoffs.
